body:
Actually, looking at this again, is it actually a bug? The assignment in line 7 is unnecessary, since `foo` is never used afterwards. (The line could be replaced with just `bar(foo);` and the rule would pass.)

I suppose it is a bit misleading to report an error on line 3 instead of line 7, though.

The left side of the final assignment expression is unnecessary, but the variable is "used", at least according to my interpretation of the rule. You can look at the linked StackOverflow question for a less trivial example. In an ideal world (and I believe this is what you were getting at when you suggested warning on line 7 instead of the declaration), we'd be able to determine statically that the result of the final assignment expression is unused and suggest using the right side by itself. Even supposing that were possible (it may be, and that be really cool), I don't think that warning should come from no-unused-vars. Put another way, my interpretation of no-unused-vars is that when it declares a variable as unused, I ought to be able to remove that variable from my program without changing the program's behavior. Does that fit?

Also, welcome to the team! :tada:

I think the current version of the rule _does_ try to determine statically that the last assignment is unused, and that's why it reports an error in this case. (In the StackOverflow question, the line `stream = stream.pipe(gulp.dest(manifestRoot));` can be replaced with `stream.pipe(gulp.dest(manifestRoot));` without changing anything)

Perhaps the name `no-unused-vars` is a bit misleading (could be `no-unused-assignments` instead), but I think the ability to lint for unused assignments is very useful. In lieu of creating another rule to check for unused assignments, I think it would be better to keep this error and improve the error message (i.e. ensure that it's on the right line, and that the message more accurately describes the issue).
Also, there is a document issue: #6703

So I propose we make the following changes:
- ~~We should report every case where an unused assignment happens. (At the moment, we only report it in one place -- where the variable was declared.)~~
- We should improve the error message in cases like this (e.g. `Unused assignment to variable 'foo'`).
@nzakas I thought this is the intentional behavior of #6348 and this is a duplicate of #6703. I'm sorry if I overlook anything.

I'm not sure that the point of the rule is to detect that the most recent assignment of a variable is useless, if the variable was used (on an RHS, and not as part of a self-assign) before that assignment.

Seems we should be able to use code path analysis to determine if a variable has been used before being assigned to.

Am I missing something?

@not-an-aardvark I'm open to changing the message that's reported in order to avoid confusion in those cases. Maybe something like "foo is assigned a value but is never used" instead?

@mysticatea no need to apologize. It's just that you didn't leave a comment explaining why you removed "accepted," so I wasn't sure if you disagreed that this was a bug, or something else.
